newsitem.title: UK: Shorts announce 120 new jobs in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Shorts announce 120 new jobs in Northern Ireland.

text.p: Short Brothers Plc, the Northern Ireland-based subsidiary of Bombardier Inc, said on Thursday it is creating 120 jobs to keep pace with demands for aircraft composite components.

"As a result of recent increases in the aircraft production rates of our major customers, there is a need to employ a further 120 production line employees at our two composite plants," Ken Brundle, vice president and general manager, aerospace, said in a statement.
Shorts has two advanced composite production plants at Newtownabbey and Dunmurry on the outskirts of Belfast.
It employs some 6,000 at its Belfast plants, and 3,000 abroad.
"Composites is an area of our business which has experienced very significant growth in recent years," Brundle said.

"The horizontal stabiliser for the Bombardier Global Express, one of the largest and most technologically advanced composite structures fitted to any commercial aircraft, is a good example of our capability," he said.
Others include the Boeing 737 rudder and composite components for Roll-Royce engines on Boeing 757 aircraft, Brundle added.
Around 850 Shorts jobs were lost and a further 150 are to go as a result of the bankruptcy of Dutch aircraft firm Fokker, one of its main customers earlier this year.
But a Shorts spokesman said medium-term employment prospects "are very good indeed" due to an upturn in confidence within the aircraft manufacturing industry.
"We are seeing now aircraft manufacturers like Boeing increasing production rates. That feeds through to suppliers like us who consequently have to keep pace." the spokesman told Reuters.

Montreal, Canada-based Bombardier Inc, which has 40,000 employees internationally, specialises in designing, manufacturing and marketing in the fields of transportation equipment, civil and military aerospace and motorised consumer products.
